svg.data-vd-steps: [[0, "The periodic table: 118 elements in order of atomic number, in 7 periods (rows) and 18 groups (columns)."], [1, "Alkali metals (group 1): Soft, very reactive metals with one outer electron; react with water to give hydrogen and an alkaline solution."], [2.6, "Alkaline earth metals (group 2): Reactive metals with two outer electrons."], [4.2, "Transition metals: Hard, dense metals; often coloured compounds, several ions (e.g. Fe\u00b2\u207a, Fe\u00b3\u207a) and useful as catalysts."], [5.8, "Post-transition metals: Softer metals such as aluminium, tin and lead."], [7.4, "Metalloids: Properties between metals and non-metals; silicon and germanium are semiconductors."], [9, "Reactive non-metals: Hydrogen, carbon, nitrogen, oxygen, phosphorus, sulfur and selenium."], [10.6, "Halogens (group 17): Reactive non-metals with seven outer electrons; exist as diatomic molecules (F\u2082, Cl\u2082, Br\u2082, I\u2082)."], [12.2, "Noble gases (group 18): Full outer shells, so very unreactive; monatomic gases."], [13.8, "Lanthanoids: f-block metals of period 6."], [15.4, "Actinoids: f-block metals of period 7; all radioactive."]]
svg.title: The periodic table
svg.desc: The periodic table of 118 elements, coloured by category: alkali metals, alkaline earth metals, transition metals, post-transition metals, metalloids, non-metals, halogens, noble gases, lanthanoids and actinoids.
svg.text: Atomic number above each symbol. The f-block (lanthanoids and actinoids) is shown below the main table.

g.data-info: Soft, very reactive metals with one outer electron; react with water to give hydrogen and an alkaline solution.
Reactive metals with two outer electrons.
Hard, dense metals; often coloured compounds, several ions (e.g. Fe²⁺, Fe³⁺) and useful as catalysts.
Softer metals such as aluminium, tin and lead.
Properties between metals and non-metals; silicon and germanium are semiconductors.
Hydrogen, carbon, nitrogen, oxygen, phosphorus, sulfur and selenium.
Reactive non-metals with seven outer electrons; exist as diatomic molecules (F₂, Cl₂, Br₂, I₂).
Full outer shells, so very unreactive; monatomic gases.
f-block metals of period 7; all radioactive.
Columns. Elements in the same group have the same number of outer-shell electrons, so similar chemical properties.
Rows. Elements in the same period have the same number of occupied electron shells.
The staircase separates metals (left, most elements) from non-metals (right). Metalloids lie along it.
